findings.what:
The v3 s_merge assumption 'Lab gains transfer when the change does not lean on network confidence', and the same anchor in 'sub-voxel localisation closed in practice' and in I-029 (z shift).
OLD VERDICT: OVERTURNED. The anchor was probes 32/33: float output with 'safe' encoding had a lab gain of +0.0019 on 199 videos but tied its int parent on the LB twice. The same ties were reason (4) in R8-RC-A's skeptic refutation of the +0.1 vox z shift ('coordinate-only lab gains read 0 on the LB 3 times').
WHAT CHANGED: (1) Discussion 744093 (Hammad Farooq, 16:29Z): the same 0.954 graph with round(v,3) floats scored 0.946 (-0.008). A scorer that read Float64 could not lose 0.008 on sub-voxel-better coordinates, so the Kaggle scorer casts floats to integers, probably by truncation. Our safe encoding is w = max(0, r + min(max(round(v-r,3),0),0.499)) with r = round(v). That gives floor(w) == round(w) == r, so under ANY integer-casting scorer the safe CSV is equivalent to the int CSV. Probes 32/33 therefore tied BY CONSTRUCTION. They were never a test of lab transfer. (2) MEASURED on CPU: I emulated 744093's transform on the exp60 x138 lab (56 clips, official metric; 100% of nodes have non-integer coordinates). floor(z,y,x) vs round: ALL -0.00498 (TP -80, FP +139); 44b6 -0.01310; 6bba -0.00425. By axis: floor_z alone -0.00386, floor_yx alone -0.00066 (44b6 -0.0061, 6bba -0.0002). The LB's -0.008 (display step, true value about -0.007..-0.009) lies between the two train-embryo lab values. That makes it one clean magnitude calibration of this lab for a pure geometric transform on the public embryo.
NEW VERDICT: the float anchor is VOID, not negative. The overturn stands only for confidence-leaning changes (edge filter +0.016 lab -> 0 LB). For geometry, the lab is calibrated in magnitude for large perturbations. Small (+-0.002) geometric gains remain sign-noisy on 4-clip beds (see R28-RC-C). On the z shift (I-029), reason (4) of the R8 refutation falls. The other reasons stand: the bias is embryo-dependent (post-head z bias 44b6 +0.15 um vs 6bba +0.45 um); Canh's constant xyz correction lost 0.0031 on the LB; on the CI bed z+0.1 on top of CI was -0.00085 (R25); it needs new writer code on the path of our best file; and it is outside the user's 12:25Z/14:12Z morning depth cap {K, SEC, DIS 2.25, CI}. It STAYS post-deadline, with nothing built tonight. The 16:39Z line 'float output stays closed' is right, now for the correct reason: the scorer has no sub-voxel channel.

The EXP75 PARTNER RULE v2 and the choice of exp75 (#37 + CI) as the private hedge rest on that prior.
NEW MEASUREMENT: I scored the dummy lab (4 other train clips, in-sample for the refiners, which saw 171/199 stems). CI loses on all 3 like-for-like pairs: exp79a-exp70g -0.00549 (TP -4, FP +9, FN +4); exp87a-exp85a -0.00509; exp75-exp58 -0.00549. Both 6bba dummy clips lose 2 TP each, and the 44b6 clips are unchanged. On the same clips CI still LOWERS the matched 3D error on 3/4 (6bba_05b6 1.908 -> 1.755 um, 6bba_05db 1.474 -> 1.356, 44b6_0113 0.990 -> 0.772; 44b6_0b24 2.386 -> 2.435). So the variance cut is real (7/8 clips across the two beds), but it does not turn into edges monotonically. The pooled in-sample edge evidence is now mixed: CI bed +0.0032, dummy clips -0.0055. The positive evidence left is one public-embryo LB read.
NEW VERDICT: R25-RC-C is PARTLY OVERTURNED. The 'public-only' label stays removed (the LB read is out of embryo), but the prior is too high. Revised: P(>=0 on private) ~0.55-0.65, central ~+0.0002, sd ~0.001. That is still above mc26's break-even for pair B over A (private CI mean > ~-0.0002 at sd 0.0008, ~-0.0004 at sd 0.0015).
